processing: A cultivar bred for sencha, normally steamed, rolled and dried in the usual way.
harvest_season: A normal-budding cultivar picked one or two days later than Yabukita; the spring flush is the prized one, as usual for sencha.
appearance_dry: As sencha, typically deep green needles.
appearance_liquor: A clear, attractive green-tinted yellow, as the cultivar keeps a good green colour when made into sencha.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf, typical of a steamed sencha.
taste_profile: Refreshing, sweet aroma over a balanced but light flavour, with more amino acids and fewer catechins than Yabukita.

brewing.notes: A light tea that is easily overwhelmed: use a moderate amount of leaf and keep the steeps short.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring sencha, mostly from small producers offering it by cultivar. As with other sencha it is best within about a year of picking, and it has no ageing value.
description:
Harumoegi is a Japanese sencha cultivar from Miyazaki Prefecture. It is known for a light, fragrant cup, and its name is often translated as yellowish-green spring.

It goes through the normal sencha process, so its character comes from the plant. It holds a good green colour once made into sencha, and it has more amino acids and fewer catechins than Yabukita, which points to a gentler cup.

The aroma is the main attraction: refreshing and sweet, on a light and balanced body. Too much leaf or very hot water pushes it out of balance, so keep things moderate.

You are not likely to see it unless a shop sells by cultivar, and it is rarely a headline name. With a harvest date and a producer on the label, you are looking at the real thing.

It grows well across most of Japan since it handles cold about as well as Yabukita, so try lots from different regions if you can find them.
history:
Harumoegi was bred at the Miyazaki Prefecture Agricultural Experiment Station from a 1981 cross of Chamoto F1NN27 and ME52. Chamoto F1NN27 goes back to a 1953 cross of Yabukita and Shizuoka Zairai 16, and ME52 is a native Miyazaki plant selected in 1932.

The best seedling was registered in 2003. Its yield is about the same as Yabukita's.
sources_note: One listing also shows a 2006 registration entry; the 2003 date is from the most detailed account. name_zh is a plain rendering, not an established Chinese name.
